But `TableCell.style` is equally required by the model (packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:498) and is read without a guard *before* `body` ever is: `paddingOf` does `const p = cell.style.padding` (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/table-renderer.ts:581), called at table-renderer.ts:106 during layout, and `paintCellFills` does `cell.style.fill` at table-renderer.ts:203. `migrateElement` repairs nothing but shape fills (packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts:155-168), so nothing fixes it on read. verdict.reason: Verified independently. `TableCell.style` is required (packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:498) and is dereferenced without any guard by `paddingOf` (table-renderer.ts:581), reached from `computeTableLayout` (table-renderer.ts:106,124) which `drawTable` calls first (table-renderer.ts:44) — before `cell.body` is ever touched — plus `paintCellFills` (table-renderer.ts:203). `drawTable` is on the real render path via element-renderer.ts:356, and `computeTableLayout` from six editor call sites (editor.ts:1150,3615,3832,4305,5526,7127). Nothing repairs an absent style on read: `migrateElement` early-returns for every non-shape element (migrate.ts:155-156), the frontend read path uses only migrateDocument/migrateMeta (yorkie-slides-store.ts:457,472), and readSlidesRoot/writeSlidesRoot pass slides through verbatim (slides-tree.ts:60-110). The new repair (docs-content.controller.ts:646-669) fills only `body` (line 661) and never inspects `cell.style`, while the docs arm of the same file does validate cell style (line 410) and the slide-text arm fills block/inline style (lines 747, 833). So a payload cell of `{}` is accepted and stored in a shape that throws a TypeError for every viewer — a real crash/data-integrity gap in the correctness lane. No counterexample found anywhere in model, store, migrate, importer, Yorkie tree, or renderer.

finding.summary: New slides walk early-returns on an absent/non-object element `data`, so a text element with no `data` is persisted in the exact shape that crashes every viewer
finding.evidence: `assertValidElementData` line 617: `const data = e.data as ...; if (!data || typeof data !== 'object') return;`. A payload element `{ id:'e1', type:'text', frame:{} }` therefore passes `assertValidElement` and reaches `writeSlidesRoot`, which stores it verbatim. Readers dereference unconditionally: `drawText` → `isTextBodyEmpty(data)` → `isBlocksEmpty(data.blocks)` → `blocks.length` (packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:653) throws on undefined; `migrateElement` (packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts:156) bails for anything that is not a shape, so nothing repairs it on read. This is the same failure mode the new `assertValidTextBodyBlocks`/`normalizeSlideInlines` repair path exists to prevent (it fills `blocks`/`inlines`/`style` in), just reached one level higher. The same early return also means `data: []` (an array is `typeof 'object'`) gets the repair written as an array expando (`[].blocks = []`) that is dropped on JSON serialization, so the 'repaired' body is not what gets stored.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts assertValidElementData early-returns for a text element whose `data` is absent/non-object, letting `{id,type:'text',frame:{}}` reach writeSlidesRoot verbatim, and that `data: []` gets an array-expando repair. Both are false in the current code. packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:625-638 handles `e.type === 'text'` BEFORE the generic early return: absent/null `data` is repaired in place to `{ blocks: [] }` (line 627-630), and a non-object OR array `data` throws BadRequestException (line 631-635) rather than being repaired — the comment at 612-619 states this is deliberate exactly because a JSON-dropped array expando would leave the crashing shape stored. The `const data = ...; if (!data || typeof data !== 'object') return;` line the reviewer quoted is line 639-640 and is reachable only for non-text types (shape/table/group), which have their own body handling (e.g. absent TableCell.body filled at 661, nested children re-walked at 673). Because `e.data` is set to `{blocks: []}` before persistence, the claimed reader crash isElementEmpty -> isBlocksEmpty(el.data.blocks) (packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:640,651-655) cannot fire from this path. The guard runs on the write path ahead of writeSlidesRoot (controller line 193) via assertValidSlidesBody -> assertValidSlide (553) -> assertValidElement (580) -> assertValidElementData, and layout/group elements reach the same function via assertValidNestedElement (599).

finding.summary: Slide block with no `style` is accepted, but the PPTX exporter dereferences `block.style` unconditionally
finding.evidence: `assertValidSlideBlocks` only validates `style` when it is present (`if (block.style !== undefined && block.style !== null)`, line 694) — deliberately, per the doc comment. But `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:99` does `ALGN.get(block.style.alignment)` and lines 105/107/113/119/122 read `block.style.marginLeft/textIndent/lineHeight/marginTop/marginBottom` with no guard, so a stored block without `style` throws during PPTX export of that deck. The canvas path survives only because `text-renderer.ts` normalizes styles first; the export path does not. Same class as the `inlines` repair — either repair `block.style = {}` or reject.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `assertValidSlideBlocks` only validates `style` when present, leaving a block with absent `style` to crash the PPTX exporter at `blockToXml`. The cited condition does not exist: a grep for `style !== undefined && ... style !== null` across packages/backend/src/api/v1 returns no matches, and line 694 is inside a doc comment, not code. The actual code at docs-content.controller.ts:740-747 implements exactly the repair the finding prescribes: `if (block.style === undefined || block.style === null) { block.style = {}; } else { /* type check + assertValidBlockStyle */ }` — with an inline comment naming the very sink in question (`ALGN.get(block.style.alignment)` in packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts) as its motivation. The repair covers every path into the sink: slide notes (:557), text bodies (:723 via assertValidTextBodyBlocks), and recursively nested docs-table cell blocks (:770). The sink itself is accurately described — text.ts:99 and 105/107/112/119/122 do dereference block.style unguarded — but no stored block can reach it with an absent style, so the crash path does not exist. This mirrors the adjacent `inline.style = {}` repair at :833 that the finding itself cites as the model to follow.
